title: Mitä: asking and answering about actions and objects
summary: Mitä is the partitive form of mikä. Mitä sinä juot? — Juon vettä.
targetSkills: Mitä: asking and answering about actions and objects
objectives: Ask about an activity or partitive object with mitä.
Give the requested activity or object in a natural reply.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns.
Plural means more than one in this grammatical pattern.
A stem is the part of a word to which an ending is attached.
The partitive is a word form used here for an amount, an action's object, or a substance or group description.
A weak stem uses the changed consonants shown in the construction steps; the strong stem keeps the corresponding strong consonants.

Mitä is the partitive form of mikä. It asks about the thing in these familiar action patterns: Mitä juot? (“What are you drinking?”). Mitä teet? asks what activity you are doing. The complete verb forms are provided.
keyPoints: Do not substitute mikä in these partitive object questions.

sections.title: Answering the question
paragraphs: Answer with the corresponding activity or object, not kyllä (“yes”). Here juoda (“drink”) and syödä (“eat”) describe an unspecified amount, and lukea (“read”) describes an activity in progress, so the object uses the partitive. Use vettä (“water”), leipää (“bread”) and kirjaa (“a book”) in these bounded situations.
A natural short reply to “Mitä sinä juot?” is “Vettä.” (“Water.”). Use the full reply when it makes the person, action or correction clearer.
To correct an offered drink, reject it and then name what you are drinking. The complete negative phrase en juo means I am not drinking; the supplied object forms stay partitive.
The exercises show supporting Finnish words and their meanings when recalling them is not the task. Read the complete English meaning before choosing the question or answer form.
keyPoints: Give the activity or object requested by mitä; a yes/no reply does not supply that information.

sections.title: Build the answer forms
paragraphs: vettä means water here. Vesi has the irregular singular partitive vettä. Learn this common form directly.
leipää means bread here. Leipä keeps p and adds -ä: leipää.
kirjaa means a book here. Kirja + -a gives kirjaa, the singular partitive used for the reading activity in progress.
kahvia means coffee here. Kahvi + -a gives kahvia, an unspecified amount of coffee.
Luen means I read here. Lukea removes final -a, drops k in the weak stem, and adds -n: lue- + -n gives luen.
keittoa means soup here. Keitto keeps strong tt and adds -a: keittoa.
mehua means juice here. Mehu + -a gives mehua.
Juomme means we drink here. Juo- + -mme gives juomme.
puuroa means porridge here. Puuro + -a gives puuroa.
lehteä means a newspaper here. Lehti uses the stem lehte- with -ä: lehteä.
teetä means tea here. Tee + -tä gives teetä, with a front-vowel ending after neutral e.
syö means eat here. Syödä removes -dä to form syö, used as the singular third-person affirmative form or as the main verb after a negative verb.

sinä: you; subject (who or what this sentence is about). Sinä addresses one person informally.
juot: you drink; verb (the action or state). Juo- + singular second-person -t gives juot.

examples.english: I am not drinking water. I am drinking coffee.
steps: En: I do not; negative verb (marks not and identifies the person). En is the first-person singular negative verb. The main verb takes its negative form.

juo: drink; main verb after the negative verb. Juoda removes -da to form juo. This is the singular third-person affirmative form and, after a negative verb, the negative main-verb form; the long vowel does not lengthen further.
vettä: water; object (the thing the action concerns). Vesi has the irregular singular partitive vettä. Learn this common form directly.
Juon: I drink; verb (the action or state). Juoda removes -da and adds -n: juo- + -n gives juon.
kahvia: coffee; object (the thing the action concerns). Kahvi + -a gives kahvia, an unspecified amount of coffee.
